A LITTLE MATH GOES A LONG WAY.

Time’s up.

0HEXES PLACED

SIX IN YOUR HAND. ROOM TO GROW.

Make every triangle count.

  1. Choose your center.

    The six tiles around it are random, checked so all six starting triangles work. Your hand contains six random digits.

  2. Make a valid triangle.

    A triangle is three hexes that all touch each other. Any two digits must add to the third, keeping only the last digit. For example, 3 + 4 = 7, or 8 + 7 = 15 → 5. Zero and repeated digits are allowed.

  3. Check every triangle you complete.

    Choose a hand tile and an outlined hex beside two touching tiles. Your placement must make every triangle it completes valid. You can build around the whole board, not just the last tile.

  4. Beat your own score.

    Each valid placement scores one hex and replaces the used hand tile with one random digit. Wrong placements use a mistake; they don’t consume your tile. The round ends at the time or mistake limit. Hints and hand swaps cost 10 seconds when timed.
